preamble: In the Outer Hebridean dialects of Scottish Gaelic, especially Lewis, the palatalized ('slender') rhotic /ɾʲ/ is commonly pronounced as the voiced dental fricative [ð]. The rhotic loses its tap closure and becomes a continuous dental fricative, while the following or preceding front vowel carries the palatal quality. Other dialects treat slender r differently: southern Barra has [ʒ] and Tiree has [j] or [i̯]. Outside Gaelic this development is rare.

examples.note: Slender r is often produced as a dental fricative in Lewis and in other Outer Hebridean dialects.
Word-final slender r, contrasting with broad r in car 'somewhat' /kʰaɾ/.
